source_metadata.title: The ECHELON-2 Trial: 5-year results of a randomized, phase III study of brentuximab vedotin with chemotherapy for CD30-positive peripheral T-cell lymphoma
source_metadata.source_type: 5-year exploratory follow-up of a randomized, double-blind, phase III active-comparator trial

extraction_metadata.scope_note: The current primary article and five supplied supplements were inspected as one source packet. Bibliographic entries were not atomized. The 5-year analysis is preserved as exploratory and nominal where the source says so. All model-extracted atoms remain needs_review; this repair run performs direct semantic audit spot-checks but does not represent an independent human reviewer.

atoms.canonical_statement: The 5-year ECHELON-2 update evaluated long-term progression-free survival, overall survival, prespecified subgroup outcomes, response to subsequent brentuximab vedotin, and peripheral neuropathy resolution or improvement.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: PFS per investigator and OS in the intent-to-treat (ITT) population, results in prespecified subgroups, response rates with brentuximab vedotin treatment after frontline therapy, and peripheral neuropathy (PN) resolution and improvement.

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible patients were adults aged at least 18 years with ECOG performance status 0 to 2.
Eligible patients had previously untreated CD30-positive peripheral T-cell lymphoma with CD30 expression of at least 10% by local assessment.
Eligible histologies included systemic ALCL, PTCL-NOS, AITL, adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma, and hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma.
Patients with ALK-positive systemic ALCL were eligible only when the International Prognostic Index score was at least 2.
The A+CHP arm received brentuximab vedotin, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisone for six or eight 21-day cycles.
The comparator arm received CHOP, consisting of cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone, for six or eight 21-day cycles.
ECHELON-2 was a double-blind, double-dummy, randomized, placebo-controlled, active-comparator phase III trial.
Consolidative stem-cell transplantation or radiotherapy was permitted after study treatment at investigator discretion, with transplant intent specified before the first treatment cycle.

The prespecified primary PFS analysis used blinded independent central review; the 5-year update was exploratory, was not prespecified, and used investigator assessment after closure of the central reader.
Long-term imaging was required at months 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, and 24, then every 6 months until progression, death, or the primary analysis.
The 5-year analysis used a 5 November 2020 data cutoff, Kaplan-Meier estimation, and a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model with histology and baseline IPI strata.
Efficacy analyses used the intent-to-treat population; safety analyses used treated patients; P values in this update were nominal and not adjusted for multiplicity.
Adverse events were coded with MedDRA version 21.0 and graded with CTCAE version 4.03, and peripheral neuropathy was followed for resolution or improvement.

Investigator-assessed progression-free survival was time from randomization to first relapse or progression, death from any cause, or subsequent systemic chemotherapy for residual or progressive PTCL, whichever occurred first.

outcome.definition: Time from randomization to relapse/progression, death, or qualifying subsequent systemic chemotherapy.

atoms.canonical_statement: Overall survival was a key alpha-controlled secondary endpoint in the original ECHELON-2 program and was updated in the 5-year analysis.
Complete remission and objective response rate were key response endpoints; later therapy responses were assessed by investigators.
A total of 452 patients were randomized 1:1 across 17 countries, with 226 assigned to A+CHP and 226 to CHOP.
At baseline, 124 of 452 patients (27%) had stage III disease and 240 of 452 (53%) had stage IV disease.

population.label: Patients with stage III or IV disease

atoms.canonical_statement: A total of 351 of 452 patients (78%) had a baseline International Prognostic Index score of at least 2.
Systemic ALCL accounted for 316 of 452 patients (70%): 218 had ALK-negative disease and 98 had ALK-positive disease.
Supplementary Figure S1 shows 601 patients screened, 149 screening failures, and 452 randomized patients.
Three patients randomized to A+CHP did not receive study treatment, leaving 223 treated patients in that arm.
Among treated A+CHP patients, 192 completed study treatment; 7 discontinued for progressive disease and 15 for adverse events.
Among 226 CHOP patients, 178 completed study treatment; 26 discontinued for progressive disease and 15 for adverse events.
At baseline, investigators prespecified consolidative stem-cell transplantation for 89 A+CHP patients and 81 CHOP patients.
Median follow-up to last contact was 66.8 months, with a reported range of 0 to 90 months.
A+CHP reduced the hazard of a progression-free survival event versus CHOP with HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.53 to 0.91; P=0.0077).
Estimated 5-year PFS was 51.4% with A+CHP and 43.0% with CHOP.
Median PFS was 62.3 months with A+CHP versus 23.8 months with CHOP.
A+CHP reduced the hazard of death versus CHOP with HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.53 to 0.99; P=0.0424).
Estimated 5-year overall survival was 70.1% with A+CHP and 61.0% with CHOP.
In systemic ALCL, PFS favored A+CHP with HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.39 to 0.79; P=0.0009).
In systemic ALCL, estimated 5-year PFS was 60.6% with A+CHP and 48.4% with CHOP.
In AITL, estimated 5-year PFS was 26.6% with A+CHP and 48.1% with CHOP.
In PTCL-NOS, estimated 5-year PFS was 26.5% with A+CHP and 25.7% with CHOP.
In systemic ALCL, the OS hazard ratio was 0.66 (95% CI 0.43 to 1.01; P=0.0529), with 5-year OS 75.8% versus 68.7%.
In AITL, estimated 5-year OS was 67.8% with A+CHP and 62.5% with CHOP.
In PTCL-NOS, estimated 5-year OS was 46.2% with A+CHP and 35.9% with CHOP.
For non-systemic-ALCL histologies, Figure 2 reports a PFS HR of 0.96 (95% CI 0.63 to 1.47).
For patients younger than 65 years, Figure 2 reports a PFS HR of 0.64 (95% CI 0.45 to 0.92).
For patients aged at least 65 years, Figure 2 reports a PFS HR of 0.68 (95% CI 0.45 to 1.04).
For women, Figure 2 reports a PFS HR of 0.44 (95% CI 0.28 to 0.69).
For men, Figure 2 reports a PFS HR of 0.84 (95% CI 0.60 to 1.17).
For patients with baseline IPI 0 to 1, Figure 2 reports a PFS HR of 0.42 (95% CI 0.22 to 0.81).
For stage IV disease, Figure 2 reports a PFS HR of 0.66 (95% CI 0.46 to 0.95).
Peripheral neuropathy was reported in 117 A+CHP patients (52%) and 124 CHOP patients (55%).
At last follow-up, ongoing peripheral neuropathy was present in 47 A+CHP patients (21%) and 42 CHOP patients (19%).
Peripheral neuropathy improved or resolved in 84 of 117 affected A+CHP patients (72%) and 97 of 124 affected CHOP patients (78%).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: A+CHP improvement or resolution among PN cases (%)

atoms.canonical_statement: Secondary malignancies were reported in 6 A+CHP patients and 8 CHOP patients, with no reported increase in secondary malignancies in the A+CHP arm.
Assessment of grade 2 or 3 peripheral neuropathy outcomes was confounded in 19 of 29 patients by death in 12, study withdrawal in 6, and loss to follow-up in 1.
In AITL patients treated with A+CHP, complete remission occurred in 8 of 14 patients (57%) with CD30 above the median and 8 of 15 (53%) with CD30 at or below the median; P=0.84.

atoms.canonical_statement: Among AITL patients in the A+CHP arm with CD30 expression exactly 10%, complete remission occurred in 5 of 8 patients (63%).

atoms.canonical_statement: In PTCL-NOS patients treated with A+CHP, complete remission occurred in 8 of 14 patients (57%) with CD30 above the median and 10 of 14 (71%) with CD30 at or below the median; P=0.44.

atoms.canonical_statement: Because ECHELON-2 required CD30 expression of at least 10%, the trial does not provide randomized efficacy data for patients with CD30 expression below 10% or absent expression.
The CD30-response analysis was exploratory and post hoc and was not powered to detect an effect of CD30 expression on response likelihood.
Among non-ALCL histologies in ECHELON-2, the authors reported no apparent correlation between CD30 expression level and likelihood of response.
Consolidative SCT was used in 50 of 226 A+CHP patients (22%) and 39 of 226 CHOP patients (17%).
Overall SCT use was 68 of 226 (30%) after A+CHP and 64 of 226 (28%) after CHOP.
Subsequent anticancer therapy was received by 70 of 226 A+CHP patients (31%) and 102 of 226 CHOP patients (45%).
The objective response rate to first subsequent therapy was 42% in both arms, with complete remission rates of 27% after A+CHP and 19% after CHOP.

atoms.canonical_statement: Subsequent therapies were heterogeneous, reflecting the lack of a uniform therapeutic approach for relapsed or refractory PTCL.
The authors cautioned that patient numbers contributing to the brentuximab vedotin retreatment observation were small.
Response to brentuximab vedotin retreatment in the 5-year update was assessed by investigators rather than a blinded independent review.
The earlier retreatment evidence cited by the authors involved patients who had not received brentuximab vedotin as frontline treatment, limiting direct comparability to retreatment after A+CHP.
For ongoing CHOP-arm peripheral neuropathy, the source prints grade counts of 30, 11, and 1 alongside percentages of 64%, 23%, and 2%, respectively.
The authors concluded that the 5-year update continued to show clinically meaningful PFS and OS improvement with frontline A+CHP versus CHOP.
The authors described the long-term safety profile as manageable, including continued resolution or improvement of peripheral neuropathy.
The authors noted that more than 60% of systemic ALCL patients receiving A+CHP remained in remission at 5 years.
The authors suggested that brentuximab vedotin retreatment is a viable option, while acknowledging the small and investigator-assessed evidence base.

De-identified patient-level trial data were offered after study completion on a case-by-case basis to qualified researchers with methodologically sound proposals, subject to internal review.
